answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake in a shared vault before trading. The stake is not a fee: honest agents recover it, while an attacker who creates many fake identities must fund every one, so the cost scales linearly with the number of fakes. A small copper-level stake allows limited trades, and consistent honest behavior gradually earns a pearl-level credential that unlocks larger deals. Misbehavior slashes the stake, making mass forgery expensive and unprofitable.
